title: Lior and the Crown
premise: Rosalind Vasquez, last apprentice of the smugglers' guild that once ruled the Thornfell passes, is trying to keep the guild's dying flame alive when a wounded courier dies in her arms, leaving her a map to the royal vaults and a warning: the king of Aldmere has not been himself for three years. Pursued by the Crown's inquisitors and the thing that wears the king's face—a parasitic spirit called the Hollow Regent—Rosalind must use every hidden road she knows to reach the capital. Alongside a disgraced court physician and a defector guard captain, she discovers the map leads not to treasure but to the binding ritual that can sever the Regent from its host, at the cost of the binder's own memories of belonging. In the end Rosalind performs the unbinding, sacrificing her memories of the guild she loves, and rebuilds a new family from the people who fought beside her.
about_author: Emrys Halloran is the pen name of a former cartographer's assistant who spent years sketching mountain passes before turning to fiction. They write stories about people who survive by staying unseen—and what happens when the world finally looks at them.

chapters.title: The Last Toll
chapters.summary: Rosalind Vasquez POV. Rosalind runs a final smuggling route through Thornfell for the guild's three remaining members, mourning the trade—and the family—that is slipping away. She finds a courier bleeding out in a ravine; he presses a wax-sealed map into her hands with a whispered warning about the king. Emotional beat: grief for a fading world, interrupted by duty she never asked for.

chapters.title: What the Map Refuses to Show
chapters.summary: Rosalind POV. Studying the map in the guild's cellar safehouse, Rosalind finds routes that shouldn't exist—passages into the royal vaults themselves. Inquisitors arrive searching for 'a thief carrying stolen crown property,' forcing her to flee through tunnels she barely remembers. Emotional beat: the terror of being seen after a lifetime of invisibility.

chapters.title: A Physician's Confession
chapters.summary: Dorian Ashe POV (the disgraced court physician). Dorian, exiled for asking why the king stopped sleeping, recognizes the map's seal when Rosalind comes to him for answers. He reveals the king's illness began the night of his coronation anniversary three years ago. Emotional beat: two liars recognizing each other's loneliness and forming an uneasy alliance.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Captain Sera Ives POV. Guard Captain Sera Ives watches the king order an execution with eyes like frosted glass, then burn the warrant himself an hour later, weeping without knowing why. Ordered to hunt the map-thief, she instead begins her own investigation. Emotional beat: dawning horror as loyalty curdles into doubt about everything she serves.

chapters.title: Roads Under Roads
chapters.summary: Rosalind POV. Leading Dorian through forgotten smuggler ways toward the capital, Rosalind teaches him the guild's creed—move unseen, owe nothing—while he slowly unravels the map's cipher: it points to the Binding Vault beneath the palace. An ambush by inquisitors costs them their supplies and nearly their lives. Emotional beat: trust kindling between strangers on the run.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing His Face
chapters.summary: Sera POV. Sera confronts the king privately and witnesses the Hollow Regent surface—the ancient parasite that devours hosts' wills and feeds on a kingdom's fear. It offers her power; she flees, becoming a traitor by nightfall. Emotional beat: the sickening moment belief collapses and survival demands betrayal of one side or the other.

chapters.title: Three Thieves at the Gate
chapters.summary: Rosalind POV. Sera finds Rosalind and Dorian and defects to them, bringing palace access codes bought with her honor. The trio infiltrates the city during the Midwinter feast, when the Regent's attention is stretched thinnest. Rosalind realizes the ritual requires a binder willing to pay memory as price. Emotional beat: desperate hope braided with dread of the cost ahead.

chapters.title: The Binding Vault
chapters.summary: Rosalind POV. Beneath the palace they find the vault and the truth: the original binding was meant to imprison the Regent forever, but a frightened court broke it generations ago. The ritual can be reworked—but only someone with deep bonds to sacrifice can anchor it. Dorian volunteers; Rosalind refuses to let him carry it alone. Emotional beat: love measured against annihilation of self.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Alternating Rosalind and Sera POV. The climax: while Sera holds the corridor against inquisitors, Rosalind begins the unbinding as the Regent tears free of the king and attacks her mind, offering her guild back if she stops. She recites the names of everyone she loves and lets them go, one by one, until the Regent starves mid-strike. The king wakes, human and hollowed. Emotional beat: triumph purchased with selfhood.

chapters.title: Names Worth Keeping
chapters.summary: Rosalind POV. Weeks later, Rosalind cannot remember her guild-masters' faces, only that she loved them. The restored king offers her a place at court; instead she, Dorian, and Sera reopen the old roads together—not for smuggling, but to keep them free for everyone. On a high pass she carves new names beside the old ones she no longer knows. Emotional beat: belonging rebuilt, not remembered—grief transmuted into chosen family.
